name: Matrei am Brenner
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village in the Wipptal valley, home to the Bergbauernmuseum and the starting point for hikes in the Tuxer Alpen.
text:
Overview

Matrei am Brenner is a historic market town in the Innsbruck-Land district and the traditional centerpiece of the Wipptal valley. Situated at an elevation of 992 metres along the Sill River, roughly 17 kilometres south of the provincial capital Innsbruck, the town rests along the primary trans-alpine route towards the Brenner Pass. Home to approximately 1,000 residents, Matrei is celebrated for its exceptionally preserved architectural ensemble: colourful townhouses built in the traditional Inn-Salzach style featuring ornate stucco facades, bays, and wrought-iron guild signs line the market street. As Tyrol's second-oldest chartered market town, Matrei brings together rich merchant history with prime access to untouched tributary valleys.

History

Archaeological finds in the basin date back to the Hallstatt and Roman imperial eras. In antiquity, the settlement flourished as "Matreium", a major postal relay and horse-changing outpost along the Via Claudia Augusta route across the Alps. In 1251, Count Albert III of Tyrol granted Matrei official market rights, making it the second-oldest market town in historic Tyrol after Merano. Positioned along the primary commercial artery between Germany and Italy, local carters, craft guilds, and taverns prospered for centuries. The lavish parish church of the Assumption was rebuilt in rococo elegance in 1754–1755 by master builder Franz de Paula Penz, adorned with frescoes by Josef Schöpf. Nearby, the Servite monastery of Maria Waldrast stands at 1,638 metres as one of Europe's highest pilgrimage abbeys.

Getting There

Matrei am Brenner enjoys first-rate transportation connectivity. Motorists arrive via the A13 Brenner Autobahn taking the Matrei/Steinach exit, or travel toll-free from Innsbruck along the scenic B182 Brenner federal highway in approximately twenty minutes. Rail passengers benefit from direct connections on the trans-alpine Brenner Railway: Matrei am Brenner station is served every 30 minutes by Tyrolean S-Bahn trains (lines S3 and S4), offering rapid transit to Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof. Furthermore, regional buses provide regular connections into scenic side valleys such as Navis and Schmirn.

Tips

A stroll down the historic market street admiring the listed frescoed merchant houses and traditional guesthouses offers a captivating journey through alpine trade history. An excursion to the sanctuary of Maria Waldrast, nestled at the foot of Mount Serles (2,717 m), is highly recommended for its monastery church and healing mineral spring water. Mountain hikers and cyclists can explore secluded alpine pastures in the Tux and Stubai Alps. In winter, nearby ski arenas like the Bergeralm in neighbouring Steinach and panoramic toboggan runs ensure rewarding snow adventures.
